facts.text: Deciding which physical tests to keep and which to replace follows information value and extrapolation risk rather than a fixed percentage: physical tests anchor new physics, boundaries and high-consequence outcomes, while simulation fills the repetitive interior between those anchors.
facts.quote: The decision follows information value and extrapolation risk, not a fixed percentage: physical tests stay where they anchor new physics, boundaries and high-consequence outcomes, and simulation fills the repetitive interior between those anchors.

facts.text: Space and medical simulation frameworks retain physical testing where model risk is high and validation evidence is weakest; the frameworks discussed agree on the test-replacement logic but provide no numerical replacement fraction.
facts.quote: The frameworks agree on the logic though none gives a number. Space and medical practice keep physical testing where model risk is high and validation evidence weakest

facts.text: Nuclear practice allocates test data to highly ranked phenomena when deciding how to support simulation.
facts.quote: nuclear practice gives test data to highly ranked phenomena

facts.text: Aviation practice always physically tests the baseline seat and allows simulation to cover eligible variants.
facts.quote: aviation always tests the baseline seat and lets simulation cover eligible variants

facts.text: Rail practice validates the simulation model with running tests before extending the assessed conditions.
facts.quote: rail validates the model with running tests and then extends the assessed conditions

facts.text: The strongest candidates for retaining physical tests are tests that establish a new phenomenon, validate intended-domain endpoints, expose coupled failure mechanisms, verify minimum-safety-margin conditions, test new sensor placement, validate weather and contamination models, or investigate a discrepancy.
facts.quote: Physical tests are the strongest candidates to keep when they establish a new phenomenon, validate the ends of the intended domain, expose coupled failure mechanisms, verify conditions where the safety margin is smallest, test new sensor placement, validate weather and contamination models

facts.text: Simulation is strongest for interpolation within a physically anchored domain, parameter sweeps around a validated configuration, and closely related variants whose differences can be bounded.
facts.quote: Simulation is strongest for interpolation within an anchored domain, parameter sweeps around a validated configuration, and closely related variants whose differences can be bounded

facts.text: Published physical-test percentages are rare; a working document for the United Nations car braking regulation specifies 30% physical tests, whereas the adopted text leaves the percentage to agreement with the authority.
facts.quote: Published percentages are rare: a working document for the United Nations car braking regulation carries 30% physical tests, but the adopted text leaves the number to agreement with the authority

facts.text: A small-scale academic study avoided 51% to 66% of physical tests.
facts.quote: a small-scale academic study avoided 51% to 66% of physical tests

facts.text: No off-road physical-test replacement percentage exists in the evidence discussed, so the booklet plans using physical anchors rather than percentages.
facts.quote: no off-road figure exists. The booklet therefore plans in physical anchors rather than percentages

facts.text: The booklet's reasoned recommended split retains physical brake-performance and stopping-distance tests for each machine class across load, slope and surface extremes.
facts.quote: Its recommended split, a reasoned position: keep physical the brake performance and stopping distance per machine class across load, slope and surface extremes

facts.text: The booklet recommends retaining physical performance and false-positive tests required by the mining standard for each scenario class.
facts.quote: the mining standard's performance and false-positive tests per scenario class

facts.text: The booklet recommends retaining physical sensor characterization at each mounting extreme and in each degraded-visibility class.
facts.quote: sensor characterization at each mounting extreme and in each degraded-visibility class

facts.text: The booklet recommends retaining assessor-selected physical end-to-end confirmation runs, including closed-loop stops at the collision boundary.
facts.quote: end-to-end confirmation runs chosen by the assessor, including closed-loop stops at the collision boundary

facts.text: The booklet recommends using simulation to replace or densify combinatorial sweeps across layouts, angles, speeds and objects, weather intensities between physical anchors, intermediate machine sizes, and fault-injection cases.
facts.quote: Simulation replaces or densifies the combinatorial sweep across layouts, angles, speeds and objects, weather intensities between anchors, intermediate machine sizes, and fault-injection cases

facts.text: A defensible physical-test percentage for the heavy off-road collision-mitigation program cannot currently be specified; the replaceable fraction must emerge from credibility work rather than serve as an input assumption.
facts.quote: "A defensible physical-test percentage for this program cannot be specified today"; the replaceable fraction must be an output of the credibility work, not an input assumption
